definition: E0 crucifixion does not include death. E1 is proclamation before the Corinthian letter, with no absolute dating. E2 is a tradition, including Matthew’s narrated opposing story. E3 concerns sincere interpreted experiences of Cephas and one further disciple, not every listed group or external veridicality. E4 and E5 are transitions from nonbelief before to belief after. The James identity and the belief reading remain open bridges. Person and Period are finite comparison indices, not claims that all relevant history has been captured. Crucifixion means Jesus being affixed to a cross as punishment; it does not by definition establish death. Experienced marks a post-crucifixion experience interpreted as an encounter with Jesus; sincere means the subject genuinely accepted that interpretation, not that it was externally veridical. Believes means religious belief/allegiance to Jesus, not mere belief that Jesus existed, and does not by itself encode every Creed article. The before/after indices are ordered relative phases around the proposed change, with no calendar dates. The two disciples in E3 are distinct constructors; no universal claim about every apostle or the reported five hundred is encoded.
note: Comparison vocabulary needed to expose the limited pilot encoding and prevent report/event or consistency/truth conflation. Historical research and sourced causal theories would be needed to defend these interpretations; no modern proponent or metaphysical supplement is attributed without a witness.
